chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The hand of the man and his legs are cut in retaliation (qisas).'

key_terms.رِجْلَاهُ: His two legs, indicating the bilateral nature of the retaliation for the specific injury mentioned.
key_terms.قِصَاص: Retaliation or retribution in kind, a specific legal mechanism in Islamic jurisprudence for bodily injuries and murder.
key_terms.يَدُ الرَّجُلِ: The hand of the man, referring to the specific limb subject to amputation in this ruling.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for cutting the hand and legs in Islamic retaliation law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific application of qisas (retaliation) for intentional injury, establishing that the victim is entitled to the cutting of the perpetrator's hand and both legs as proportional retribution. In Shia jurisprudence, this narration is often discussed in the context of whether the 'hand' refers to one or both, and 'legs' to one or both, with many scholars interpreting it as the hand of the injured side and both legs to ensure exact equivalence (mu'adala). It underscores the principle of precise compensation in bodily injuries, distinct from blood money (diya).

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The hand of the man and his leg would be cut regarding the retaliation’.
